uncited: The method operates on a composed iVR-GS model consisting of multiple basic iVR-GS models.
Each basic model contains Gaussian primitives with editable attributes.
The fundamental unit of the composed model, containing Gaussian primitives with editable transfer function attributes.
It serves as the base for composing complex scenes. [Link](6685-basic-ivrgs-model.md)
A structure formed by combining multiple basic iVR-GS models to represent complex volumetric data with multiple transfer functions.
It allows for global lighting optimization. [Link](6684-composed-ivrgs-model.md)
*   **Time Complexity:** Optimization time scales with the total number of primitives.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **When to Use:** When a user wants to approximate a desired rendering effect from a single reference image without manually tuning transfer functions.
*   **When Not to Use:** When original volume data is available and direct editing is preferred; when real-time interactive editing is required without pre-computation.
It is part of the iVR-GS framework, which extends 3D Gaussian Splatting for volume visualization by allowing editable transfer functions.

It solves the problem of tedious trial-and-error transfer function adjustments by allowing the model to automatically learn the parameters required to replicate a user-provided visual effect [S1].

The claim states that the method solves the problem of tedious trial-and-error adjustments by allowing the model to automatically learn parameters to replicate a user-provided visual effect. Section 4.6 of Source [S1] explicitly states: 'This capability saves users time by eliminating tedious and inefficient trial-and-error TF adjustments.' It further explains that given a reference image (user-provided visual effect), the system freezes Gaussian attributes and learns transformation parameters for color, opacity, and lighting to approximate the intended rendering setting. This matches the claim perfectly.

*   **Output:** A transformed iVR-GS model with optimized transformation parameters for color, opacity, and lighting, capable of replicating the reference image and generating novel view synthesis (NVS) results under those learned settings [S1].

The claim states that the evidence supports a transformed iVR-GS model with optimized parameters for color, opacity, and lighting, capable of replicating the reference image and generating NVS results. Section 4.6 explicitly states: 'After training, the transformed iVR-GS model can replicate the reference image and generate accurate NVS results with the desired effect.' It further details that 'color is optimized,' 'opacity... [is] optimized,' and 'lighting is modified globally' via learnable parameters. Section 5.3 confirms the process involves optimizing these specific transformation parameters to match a reference image and then rendering novel viewpoints (NVS). Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
